newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen brokerages enjoy robust growth in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen brokerages enjoy robust growth in 1996.

text.p: Brokerage firms in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen experienced solid growth in their revenue and assets in 1996 due to the bullish local stock market, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Wednesday.
Total revenue of brokerage firms topped 6.8 billion yuan in 1996, up 60 percent from 1995, the newspaper said, quoting statistics provided by the Shenzhen Securities Firms Association.
About 38 percent of revenue came from commission charges, another 38 percent from their own stock trading and the remaining 24 percent from other business, it said. It did not elaborate.

The total assets of brokerage firms in Shenzhen stood at 41.88 billion yuan at end-1996, up 50 percent over the 1995 level, while net asset value rose 39 percent year-on-year to 5.69 billion yuan in 1996, the newspaper said.
Securities transactions conducted by the firms hit 754.3 billion yuan last year, surging 70 percent from the 1995 level, it said.
But some of the city's brokerages had high asset-to-debt ratios, which threatened their development potential, the newspaper said.
